Rashi on Bava Kamma 3b:14:1.english: The watchman said - [This means that] the Holy One, Blessed be He, said:

Rashi on Bava Kamma 3b:14:2.english: Morning has come - Redemption for the righteous.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 3b:14:3.hebrew: וגם לילה - חשך לרשעים. אם תשובו בתשובה ותבקשו מחילה, בעיו. אלמא באדם כתיב בעיו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 3b:14:3.english: And also the night - Darkness for the wicked. If you return in repentance and ask for forgiveness, [then] "ask" [be'ayu]. Thus, be'ayu is written regarding man.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 3b:15:1.hebrew: איגליין - תרגומו של נבעו, אלמא נבעו לשון גילוי. הלכך אמר מבעה זה השן, דמבעה לשון מגולה הוא, דהיינו שן, שפעמים מגולה ופעמים מכוסה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 3b:15:1.english: Were revealed - [This is] the translation of "nivu"; consequently, "nivu" is an expression of revelation. Therefore, [Shmuel] said: "Maveh, this is the tooth," for maveh is an expression of [something] revealed, that is, the tooth, which is sometimes revealed and sometimes covered.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 3b:16:1.hebrew: נבעה - דמשמע הוא עצמו נבעה, נגלה; מבעה קתני, שהוא מבעה דבר אחר:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 3b:16:1.english: Niveh - For [that] would imply [that] it itself became revealed, [i.e.,] uncovered, [whereas the mishna] teaches "maveh," which [means] that it reveals another thing.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 3b:17:1.english: Bo'eh - [This is] an expression of be'ayu [in the verse cited by Rav].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 3b:19:1.hebrew: תנא שור לקרנו ומבעה לשינו - ולקמן פריך: רגל מאי שייריה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 3b:19:1.english: [The tanna] taught "ox" for its horn and "maveh" for its tooth - And later [the Gemara] challenges: What about foot—did [the tanna] omit it?

Rashi on Bava Kamma 3b:19:2.hebrew: לא ראי הקרן שאין הנאה כו' - בעל כרחיך הכי מפרש, לא ראי הקרן שאין הנאה להזיקו כראי השן כו', כלומר, דאי כתב רחמנא קרן דחייב, לא אתיא שן מיניה, דקרן אין הנאה להזיקו, שן יש הנאה להזיקו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 3b:19:2.english: The characteristic of the horn, where there is no pleasure, etc. - Perforce, this is how it is explained: "The characteristic of the horn, where there is no pleasure in its damage, is not like the characteristic of the tooth, etc." That is to say, if the Merciful One had written [that one is] liable for the horn, the tooth would not be derived from it, for [in the case of] the horn there is no pleasure in its damage, [while in the case of] the tooth there is pleasure in its damage.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 3b:1:1.hebrew: אי דלא אפקרינהו לשמואל דאמר - התם בהמניח את הכד (לקמן בבא קמא דף כח:), כל תקלה בור הוא, ואע"ג דלא הפקיר, היינו בור:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 3b:1:1.english: If he did not declare them ownerless, according to Shmuel, who says - There, in [the chapter] "HaManiach Et HaKad" (below, Bava Kamma 28b), [that] every obstacle is a pit, and even though he did not declare [it] ownerless, it is a pit.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 3b:1:2.hebrew: ולרב דאמר - כל תקלה שלא הפקירה, משור למדנו: מה שור שהוא ממונו ואם הזיק חייב, אף כל ממונו אם הזיק חייב:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 3b:1:2.english: And according to Rav, who says - Any obstacle that [one] did not declare ownerless, we learned from Ox: Just as an ox is his property, and if it caused damage [he is] liable, so too any of his property, if it caused damage [he is] liable.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 3b:1:3.hebrew: היינו שור - ולאו תולדה דבור נינהו, ובשור אמרן לעיל תולדה דשור כי שור. ואפי' לשמואל נמי דאמר תולדה דבור נינהו, מאי חזית לאוקומי מילתא דרב פפא אתולדה דבור? מאי שנא בור דחייב, שכן תחילת עשייתו וכו':
Rashi on Bava Kamma 3b:1:3.english: These are Ox - And they are not a subcategory of Pit, and regarding Ox we said above [that] the subcategory of Ox is like Ox. And even according to Shmuel as well, who said [that] they are a subcategory of Pit, what did you see to establish Rav Pappa's statement regarding a subcategory of Pit? What is different about Pit that [one is] liable? That its initial formation [is for damage], etc.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 3b:2:1.hebrew: הני נמי תחלת עשייתן - תחילת מה שנעשו בור, דהיינו כשהונחו לשם, היו עומדים לנזק:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 3b:2:1.english: These too, their initial formation - [At] the beginning of their becoming a pit, that is, when they were placed there, they were poised to cause damage.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 3b:2:2.hebrew: וכי קאמר רב פפא - תולדה לאו כאב דידה, אתולדה דמבעה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 3b:2:2.english: And when Rav Pappa says - [That] a secondary category is not like its primary category, [he is referring] to a secondary category of Maveh.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 3b:3:1.hebrew: פלוגתא דשמואל ורב במבעה - לקמן בשמעתין:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 3b:3:1.english: The dispute between Shmuel and Rav regarding Maveh - [Is explained] later in our sugya.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 3b:4:1.english: An awake person - That is the primary category.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 3b:4:2.english: A person is forewarned - [The mishna stating] "awake and asleep" [is] at the end of Chapter 2.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 3b:5:1.hebrew: אלא - תולדה דאדם היינו כיחו וניעו. כיחו רוק הפה, ניעו ליחת החוטם (רוק היוצא מתוך גופיה אגב כח):
Rashi on Bava Kamma 3b:5:1.english: Rather - The secondary category of Man is his spittle and his phlegm. Kicho is saliva of the mouth, [and] ni'o is mucus of the nose (spittle that comes out from within his body by means of force).

Rashi on Bava Kamma 3b:5:2.hebrew: אי בהדי דאזלי מזקי - שנפל על השיראים וטנפוה, או לתוך המשקין ונמאסו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 3b:5:2.english: If while they are traveling they cause damage - [Such as] where it fell upon silk [garments] and soiled them, or into liquids and they became repulsive.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 3b:5:3.hebrew: כחו הוא - והיינו אדם גופו, וחייב:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 3b:5:3.english: It is his force - And that is [considered] the person himself, and he is liable.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 3b:5:4.hebrew: אי בתר דנייח - אחר נוח הרוק לארץ הזיקו, שהוחלק אדם בהם:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 3b:5:4.english: If after it came to rest - After the spittle came to rest on the ground, they caused damage, in that a person slipped on them.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 3b:5:5.english: Whether according to Rav or according to Shmuel, this is Pit - For this is certainly an obstacle that he made ownerless.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 3b:6:1.hebrew: ברוח מצויה - דאי ברוח שאינה מצויה הוי אונס ולא מחייב, אבל ברוח מצויה הוי תולדה דאש, שהרי אש נמי הרוח מוליכה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 3b:6:1.english: In a common wind - For if [they fell] in an uncommon wind, it would be an unavoidable accident and he would not be liable, but in a common wind, it is a derivative of Fire, for fire as well is carried by the wind.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 3b:7:1.english: That another force is involved with it - And he should have anticipated [it].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 3b:8:1.hebrew: בחצי נזק צרורות - שהיתה מהלכת והתיזה צרורות ברגליה ושיברו את הכלים, דקי"ל דהלכתא גמירי לה למשה מסיני דממונא הוא ולא קנס, ואע"ג דפלגא נזק של נגיחה הוי קנס כדאמרינן לקמן, האי פלגא נזקא ממונא הוא, והלכך לאו תולדה דקרן הוא אלא דרגל, דמכח רגל הוא דאתו, וכרגל לא הוי, דרגל משלם נזק שלם, והיינו דרב פפא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 3b:8:1.english: Regarding half-damage of pebbles - Where [an animal] was walking and kicked up pebbles with its feet and they broke utensils, as it is established for us that it is learned as a halakha to Moshe from Sinai that it is monetary compensation and not a penalty. And even though the half-damage of goring is a penalty, as we say later, this half-damage is monetary compensation. Therefore, it is not a secondary category of Horn, but of Foot, for they come about through the force of the foot; yet it is not like Foot, for Foot pays full damages, and this is [what] Rav Pappa [referred to].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 3b:9:1.english: And why is it called a secondary category of Foot - [The Gemara asks this] since it does not pay like it.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 3b:9:2.hebrew: לשלם מן העלייה - שאם הזיקה יותר ממה שהיא שוה, משלם ההיזק מביתו, כי רגל, דכתיב בה ברגל: מיטב שדהו וגו'; ולא הויא כי קרן, דאין המזיק משלם אלא מגופו, כדכתיב (שמות כ״א:ל״ה): ומכרו את השור החי וחצו את כספו, ואם הזיק יותר על כדי דמיו, מפסיד הניזק:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 3b:9:2.english: To pay from the superior-quality property - That if [the animal] caused damage [amounting to] more than it is worth, [the owner] pays the damage from his house [i.e., his personal estate], like Foot, for regarding Foot it is written: "The best of his field, etc." [Exodus 22:4]; and it is not like Horn, where the damager only pays from its body [i.e., from the animal itself], as it is written (Exodus 21:35): "and they shall sell the live ox, and divide its money," and if it caused damage in excess of its value, the injured party loses [the difference].

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 3b:12:1.hebrew: לפוטרו ברה"ר - וא"ת: אמאי פשיטא ליה טפי מלשלם מן העלייה? וי"ל: כיון דמן הדין היה משלם נזק שלם, ואתי הלכתא דלא משלם אלא חצי נזק, אם כן אתי הלכתא להקל ולא להחמיר:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 3b:12:1.english: To exempt it in the public domain - And if you say: Why is it more obvious to him [that it is to exempt it in the public domain] than [that it is] to pay from the best property? And one can say: Since by strict law [the damager] would have paid full damages, and a halakhah came [teaching] that he pays only half damages — if so, the halakhah came to be lenient and not to be stringent.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 3b:12:2.hebrew: אמאי קרי לה תולדה דרגל - אע"ג דדמי לרגל, כיון שדינה חלוק, היה לו לקרות לה שם בפני עצמה:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 3b:12:2.english: Why does he call it a derivative of foot - Even though it is similar to foot, since its legal status is different, he should have called it by a name in its own right.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 3b:15:1.hebrew: כדמתרגם רב יוסף - נקט רב יוסף, לפי שהיה בקי בתרגום, שיש כמה ענייני תרגום. ולא כדפירש בעלמא: לפי שהיה סגי נהור, ודברים שבכתב אי אתה רשאי לומר על פה, ולכך היה אומר תרגום — דמשום עת לעשות אמר התם דשרי, ואין לך עת לעשות גדול מזה:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 3b:15:1.english: As Rav Yosef translates - [The Gemara] cited Rav Yosef because he was an expert in Targum, as there are several nuances of translation. And [it is] not as was explained elsewhere: that because he was blind (sagi nahor), and written matters [of Scripture] you are not permitted to recite by heart, therefore he would recite [the] Targum — for on account of [the principle of] "a time to act" (et la'asot), it says there that it is permitted, and you have no greater "time to act" than this.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 3b:19:1.hebrew: לא ראי הקרן שאין הנאה להזיקו - ופשיעה פשע, שהיה לו לשמור שורו, שבקל היה יכול לשומרו, שאין דחוקה להזיק, כיון שאין הנאה להזיקה; אבל שן, שיש הנאה להזיקה, הוי כעין אונס, שלא היה יכול לשומרה כל כך, כיון שהשן דחוק לאכול להנאתו. ולא ראי השן, שאין כוונתו להזיק ואין יצרה תקפה, ובקל יכול לשומרה, כראי הקרן, דכוונתו להזיק ויצרה תקפה, ואין יכול לשומרה כל כך יפה:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 3b:19:1.english: The aspect of the horn, where there is no pleasure in its damaging, is not [like the aspect of the tooth] - And he committed negligence, for he should have guarded his ox, as he could easily have guarded it, since it is not driven to damage, because there is no pleasure in its damaging; but tooth, where there is pleasure in its damaging, is somewhat like an unavoidable accident, for he could not guard it as well, since the tooth is driven to eat for its pleasure. And the aspect of the tooth — where its intention is not to damage and its urge does not overpower it, and he can easily guard it — is not like the aspect of the horn, where its intention is to damage and its urge overpowers it, and he cannot guard it so well.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 3b:1:1.hebrew: משורו למדנו - היינו קרן, דשן ורגל פטורין ברה"ר. ובאבנו וסכינו אין לחלק בין תמות למועדות, דלא שייך לחלק אלא בבעלי חיים. וא"ת: היכי גמר משור? מה לשור שכן ב"ח וכוונתו להזיק! ומפרש רשב"ם, דאתי מבור ושור ממה הצד. ולקמן גבי הצד השוה, דקאמר אביי לאתויי אבנו וסכינו, לא גרס: אי לרב דאמר כולם משורו למדנו היינו שור; דלרב א"ש, דבמה הצד אתי' כדפרשי'. אבל קשה: כיון דמבור נמי יליף, לפטרו בהו כלים כבור! ולקמן בהמניח (בבא קמא דף כח.), מחייב בהו רב כלים גבי נשבר כדו:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 3b:1:1.english: We derived [them] from his ox - This means Keren (horn), for Shen (tooth) and Regel (foot) are exempt in the public domain (reshut harabbim). And regarding his stone and his knife, one cannot distinguish between tam status (tamut) and mu'ad status (mu'adot), as it is only applicable to distinguish [between them] in [the case of] living creatures. And if you say: How can he derive [them] from ox? What [is unique] about ox is that it is a living creature (ba'al chayyim) and its intention is to damage! And the Rashbam explains that it is derived from pit (bor) and ox (shor) through a common denominator (mah hatzad). And later, regarding "the common denominator" (hatzad hashaveh), where Abbaye says [it comes] to include his stone and his knife, he [Rashbam] does not have the reading: "If according to Rav, who says all of them we derived from his ox, it is ox!" For according to Rav it works out well, since it is derived through mah hatzad, as we explained. However, it is difficult: Since he also derives [it] from pit, let [one] exempt vessels regarding them, like pit! And later in [the chapter] HaManiach (Bava Kamma 28a), Rav holds [one] liable for vessels regarding [the case where] "his jug broke"!

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 3b:2:1.hebrew: וממונך - לאו דוקא גבי בור, דלאו ממונא הוא; וכן גבי אש, דפשיטא דאם הדליק גדישו של חבירו באש של אחר, דחייב:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 3b:2:1.english: And your property - [This is] not exact with regard to pit, for it is not [one's] property; and likewise with regard to fire, for it is obvious that if one kindled his fellow's grain stack with another's fire, he is liable.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 3b:4:1.hebrew: תולדה ישן - הוה מצי למפרך: דלקמן מוקי מתניתין בישן שדרכו להזיק, וקרי ליה אב; אלא דבלאו הכי, פריך שפיר:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 3b:4:1.english: [The] subcategory [is] a sleeping person - [The Gemara] could have objected that later on, [the Gemara] establishes the Mishnah [as dealing with] a sleeping person whose way is to cause damage, and calls him a primary category (av); rather, even without this, it objects well.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 3b:4:2.hebrew: והתנן אדם מועד לעולם - לא פריך דישן נמי הוי אב, כדדרש עלה בגמרא בפ' כיצד (לקמן בבא קמא דף כו:) מפצע תחת פצע; דהא לא מייתי הכא קרא, אלא מייתי דהוי כיוצא בו:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 3b:4:2.english: And didn't we learn: A person is always forewarned - [The Gemara] is not objecting that [one who is] asleep is also a primary category, as [the Gemara] expounds upon it in the Gemara in chapter Keitzad (below, Bava Kamma 26b) from "a wound for a wound" (petza tachat petza) — for it does not cite a verse here; rather, it cites [the Mishnah to show] that [the subcategory] is like it [the primary category].

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 3b:5:1.hebrew: כיחו וניעו - פירש הקונטרס: מי האף. וקשה לר"ת: דבפ' דם הנדה (נדה דף נה: ושם) קתני: כיחו וניעו ומי האף. ונראה, דכיחו הוא היוצא מן הגרון בכח, וניעו הוא היוצא מן הפה על ידי נענוע:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 3b:5:1.english: His phlegm and his spittle - The Kuntres [Rashi] explained: [That ni'o is] nasal fluid. And it is difficult to Rabbeinu Tam: For in the chapter of Dam HaNiddah (Niddah 55b, and there), [the Tanna] teaches: "His phlegm, and his spittle, and nasal fluid." And it seems that kikho is that which comes out of the throat with force (be-kho'ach), and ni'o is that which comes out of the mouth by means of movement (na'anu'a).
